clue.text: New effort needed, as nothing replaces Part 2 for chap at university

indicators.note: the second letter of the word for a university chap is swapped out for the letter standing for nothing

parts.note: a fellow is a senior member of a college
nothing is zero, the round letter O
UP means in residence at a university

explanation.surface: Someone insists a fresh attempt is needed because a university man is somehow missing a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New effort' is the definition; 'Part 2' means the second letter of the chap word, and being UP is British usage for being in residence at a university.
explanation.definitionFit: A follow-up is a further action taken after a first one, a new effort building on it.

clue.text: Loud and wild — perfect …

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
lawless means unruly, out of control

explanation.surface: Someone noisy and uncontrolled is somehow declared ideal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without a single flaw is ideal, without blemish.

clue.text: … recording one has to term fiery at the end, with reason

parts.note: a log is a written record
I is the Roman numeral one
to term something is to call it by a name

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word fiery is taken

explanation.surface: A recording artist must label something as fiery, and has a reason for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting logically means acting by sound reasoning.

clue.text: Port, old East German one, suppresses source of anarchy

indicators.note: in a down clue, pressing something under puts the letter below the rest

parts.note: Ost is German for east
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter, here of anarchy

explanation.surface: A former East German port is said to be keeping a lid on anarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: OST (German for east) and I sit on top of A, the first letter of anarchy, since in a down answer what suppresses sits above.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostia was the ancient harbour town serving Rome at the Tiber mouth.

clue.text: More work for an unpractical reformer

definitions.text: More work for an unpractical reformer

parts.words: More work for an unpractical reformer
parts.note: Sir Thomas More wrote a book describing an ideal island state; a dreamer of perfect societies takes his name from it

explanation.surface: Extra labour is demanded of a dreamy would-be reformer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' looks like 'extra', but it is Sir Thomas More, author of the 1516 book Utopia.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealist who plans impossible perfect societies is named after More's imaginary perfect island.

clue.text: Elegant type of shirt, in short sleeve variety

indicators.note: the shirt letter goes inside the rearranged sleeve letters
a variety of the letters means they are rearranged
short means the word sleeve loses its last letter

parts.note: T as in T-shirt

explanation.surface: A stylish shirt comes in a short-sleeved version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts sleeve to SLEEV, 'variety' rearranges it to SVELE, and 'in' puts T (T-shirt) inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Svelte means slender and graceful in figure.

clue.text: Aid proves tricky in very hot state?

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters are worked into a new, awkward arrangement

explanation.surface: Giving aid proves difficult in a sweltering state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' suggests a country or US state; it is a physical state of matter, and the question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid heated enough turns to gas, the condition of something boiled off.

clue.text: Put it in for non-professionals

indicators.note: the clue word it is placed inside the synonym for put

parts.note: to lay something down is to put it there

explanation.surface: An instruction to include something for the benefit of amateurs.
explanation.definitionFit: The laity are ordinary people as opposed to clergy or experts.

clue.text: Dog, delinquent at first, might finally become a young predator

indicators.note: delinquent here means failing to appear: the dog word is missing its first letter

parts.note: a beagle is a breed of hound

indicators.note: only the last letter of might is taken

explanation.surface: A dog that misbehaves early in life might end up a hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delinquent' looks like a badly behaved dog, but it means absent: BEAGLE loses B, then T from might.
explanation.definitionFit: A young bird of prey, a chick of the great raptor.

clue.text: Second post switched for the sake of possible turnover?

indicators.note: the two pieces swap places compared with the clue order

parts.note: post as a prefix means after

explanation.surface: A second delivery of mail is redirected for the sake of a business turnover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like sales; it is a fruit pastry, an example of a pudding course.
explanation.definitionFit: Afters is British slang for dessert, and a fruit turnover could be served as one.

clue.text: Gangster admits a feeling of guilt

indicators.note: the word Gangster lets the letters in, holding them inside

explanation.surface: A hoodlum owns up to feeling guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is anxiety or dread, often tinged with remorse.

clue.text: Cancelled a season for children?

parts.note: an event that is off has been called off
spring is one of the four seasons

explanation.surface: A whole season was called off for the children.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are a parent's young, sons and daughters.

clue.text: Making a profit from vital cure's development?

indicators.note: development reshapes the letters into something new

parts.note: the possessive s adds no letter

explanation.surface: A drug company makes money by developing a vital cure.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucrative venture is one bringing in money.

clue.text: Literary device used by Frost, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: rime is a coating of frost

explanation.surface: A poetic technique employed by the poet Robert Frost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frost' looks like the poet, who used rhyme; it is ice crystals, RIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Matching end sounds of lines are a standard technique of verse.

clue.text: Trick by audience's childish element

indicators.note: by means beside, so the trick word sits next to the sounded piece, after it
what an audience hears is taken by sound, not spelling

parts.note: silly means foolish, childish
a con is a swindle

explanation.surface: A trick played on a childlike audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'element' is the definition: a chemical one, not a part.
explanation.definitionFit: Silicon is a chemical element, symbol Si, used in microchips.

clue.text: Some, without hesitation, may follow fashionable shenanigans!

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: chic means stylish

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: one word wraps the other

parts.note: any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'
er is a hesitant noise

explanation.surface: Smart people get up to mischief when nobody hesitates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking but here has its old sense of outside, one piece wrapping the other; 'may follow' places the pair after the fashion word.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicanery is trickery and underhand scheming.

clue.text: Method to stop tailing heartless agent?

indicators.note: the stopping word follows behind, like someone tailing a suspect
the middle letter of the word for agent is removed

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
to stem a flow is to stop it

explanation.surface: A way of stopping a cold-hearted spy from following someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is an organised way of doing things.

clue.text: What's wrong is certain to turn up with duplicate entry

indicators.note: one word enters the other, going inside
in a down answer, turning up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: sure means certain
Roneo was a stencil duplicating machine, and to roneo is to copy

explanation.surface: Something mistaken is bound to appear when an item is entered twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duplicate' looks like a doubled entry, but it is the Roneo, an old office copying machine; 'to turn up' reverses the certain word and 'entry' puts the copier inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mistaken or incorrect is in error.

clue.text: Escape without broken heart, just like the old man!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the escape word goes round

parts.note: to fly is to flee

indicators.note: broken signals the letters of heart are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone escapes heartbreak, just like their dad did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges heart and 'without', meaning outside, wraps the escape word round it; 'the old man' is slang for one's father.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatherly means in the manner of a father, and 'the old man' is slang for one's dad.

clue.text: Farmworkers' turnover helps out a great deal

indicators.note: turning over means the remaining letters are read backwards
out means the helping word is taken out

parts.note: dairymaids work milking on farms
aids means helps

explanation.surface: Turnover of farm staff is a great help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes AIDS from DAIRYMAIDS, leaving DAIRYM; 'turnover' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A myriad is a countless number, a huge quantity.

clue.text: Boy's given name from mother — a typical Scots name

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A boy is named after his mother, using a classic Scottish name.
explanation.definitionFit: Damian is a male first name.

clue.text: A country with gold and radium

parts.note: and can mean with, together with
or is gold in heraldry
Ra is the chemical symbol for radium

explanation.surface: A nation rich in gold and radium deposits.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a tiny principality in the Pyrenees.

clue.text: A brisk instruction to produce notes on staff

definitions.text: A brisk instruction to produce notes on staff

parts.words: A brisk instruction to produce notes on staff
parts.note: notes on a staff are musical notes on a stave, and the instruction is a tempo marking telling players to go fast

explanation.surface: A boss briskly tells staff to write memos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' suggests employees and 'notes' memos; it is the musical stave.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the Italian tempo marking meaning quick and lively.

clue.text: Announced the departure of two extras?

indicators.note: two means the extra is given twice

parts.note: a bye is an extra run in cricket scored without the ball being hit

explanation.surface: Someone announces that two extras have left the film set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extras' looks like film walk-ons; in cricket a bye is an extra run.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying goodbye informally is how a leaving is announced.

clue.text: Backing precision, when disposing of car plant?

indicators.note: the letters of the word car are taken away
backing means the word is read backwards

parts.note: accuracy means precision

explanation.surface: Someone supports precision when getting rid of a car factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' reverses ACCURACY to YCARUCCA; 'disposing of' removes CAR, leaving YUCCA.
explanation.definitionFit: The yucca is a spiky-leaved desert shrub.

clue.text: Nothing's found during search of the valley

indicators.note: the letter for nothing is found in the middle of the search word

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly
nothing is zero, the round letter O

explanation.surface: Nothing turns up in a search of the valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A coomb is a short deep valley or hollow on a hillside.

clue.text: One part in a 19, perhaps, is subtracted from this

definitions.text: One part in a 19, perhaps, is subtracted from this

parts.words: One part in a 19, perhaps, is subtracted from this
parts.note: 19 across is a word for a vast number, such as a million; one part of such a whole is a tiny fraction

explanation.surface: A tiny fraction is taken away from a total.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 across is MYRIAD, a huge number; 'perhaps' says a million is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: One of a million equal parts is a minute fraction.

clue.text: Trendy. judge rises to make concluding remarks?

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means the word reads upward

parts.note: a ref, or referee, judges a game

explanation.surface: A fashionable judge stands to give closing remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' reverses REF to FER in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to draw a conclusion, and the question mark flags the punning sense.

clue.text: Recoil, and show dislike of a sweet confection aloud

parts.note: to boo is to jeer in disapproval

indicators.note: aloud means the dessert word is taken as spoken

parts.note: a meringue is a baked whipped egg-white sweet

explanation.surface: Someone flinches and loudly jeers at a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved throwing stick that comes back; figuratively, a plan that backfires on its maker.

clue.text: Lino originally put in top of house is rejected for the bottom

indicators.note: the first letter of lino is placed inside
rejected means turned back, so the roof word reads backwards

parts.note: the roof is the top of a house

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of Lino

explanation.surface: Lino first laid upstairs is thrown out and used downstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is rejected' reverses ROOF to FOOR, and 'put in' places L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The floor is the lowest surface of a room.

clue.text: Rent my robe for pre-birthday party?

indicators.note: rent means torn apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tears their robe before a birthday party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' suggests a celebration; it means a participant, someone not yet born.
explanation.definitionFit: An embryo is an unborn offspring at an early stage, so a party before its birth.

clue.text: Try-out is a disaster — it's designed for the coach trade

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in a jumble, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trial run goes badly, though it was planned for bus tours.
explanation.definitionFit: A touristy place caters for sightseers who arrive by bus.
